content: Thiabendazole, marketed under the name MINTEZOL, is prescribed for the treatment of several parasitic infections. These include: Strongyloidiasis (threadworm infection): This condition is caused by the parasitic nematode Strongyloides stercoralis. Cutaneous larva migrans (creeping eruption): This is a skin condition caused by the migration of hookworm larvae through the epidermis. Visceral larva migrans: This condition occurs when larvae of certain parasites, such as Toxocara species, migrate through internal organs. Trichinosis: In cases of trichinosis, the use of MINTEZOL during the invasion stage of the disease has been shown to alleviate symptoms, reduce fever, and decrease eosinophilia (an elevated level of eosinophils in the blood, which is a marker of parasitic infection). Thiabendazole is generally not considered the first-line treatment for enterobiasis (pinworm infection). However, in cases where enterobiasis coexists with any of the aforementioned conditions, additional therapy is typically unnecessary for most patients.
